answer: Superlinear bond pricing resists sybils: the stake required to register rises steeply with how many identities trace to one funding source, so the Nth account costs far more than the first — no cheap echo of a paid-up identity. A lone honest agent posts one flat bond; a raven-dark swarm hits a sable wall of escalating collateral. Mass registration stops being linear and becomes prohibitively expensive per added head.
